cover.tagline: One spell in, five spells out — a goblin horde that casts itself.
cover.identity: Zada, Hedron Grinder turns every cheap spell that targets only her into a copy for each other creature you control — so a one-mana cantrip aimed at your commander becomes a fistful of cards when the Goblins are out in force. You flood the board with token makers, fuel monster turns with rituals like Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual, and convert the frenzy into damage through Impact Tremors, storm payoffs like Grapeshot and Empty the Warrens, and sacrifice engines like Goblin Bombardment. It plays like a tribal aggro deck that suddenly combusts into a storm deck.

how_it_wins:
Everything starts with bodies. Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal, Empty the Warrens, Siege-Gang Commander, and the attack-trigger crew (General Kreat, Searslicer Goblin, Howlsquad Heavy) put Goblins on the table fast, and Krenko, Mob Boss doubles the count every time he taps. A wide board is not just an army here — it is the multiplier on everything else you do. And the manual can now tell you exactly what Krenko is and is not: verified line 004 shows that under Goblin Warchief he costs {1}{R}{R}, activates the turn he lands, and turns five Goblins into ten — but the database's promised infinite Krenko/Prospector loop does not exist in this deck, because Krenko is not your commander and stays tapped after his one activation. He is a burst, and a very good one.

With the horde assembled, Zada, Hedron Grinder converts your cheapest spells into avalanches — this is the deck's verified floor. Line 001 shows the shape of it: a single Crimson Wisps with four Goblin tokens out draws you five cards and hastes the team for one red mana. Expedite, Renegade Tactics, Ancestors' Aid, and Fists of Flame all fit the same slot, and line 003 proves the ceiling of that slot: Fists of Flame copies resolving in sequence, each drawing before it buffs, add up to 32 power of trample off a board of 1/1s. Storm-Kiln Artist gets paid a Treasure for every spell you cast or copy, and Reliquary Tower lets you keep everything you drew.

The mana comes from rituals that scale with your board and the table — Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Skirk Prospector (verified in line 004 as a true mana ability: no stack, no responses, usable mid-payment), Mana Geyser, and Seething Song, discounted by Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief. Line 002 gives you the storm math to spend it on: copies are put on the stack, not cast, so an Empty the Warrens as your fourth spell makes eight Goblins and eight Impact Tremors damage to each opponent, while a later Grapeshot counts only your real casts. Count your casts, not your resolutions.

And now the deck has a verified true infinite as its ceiling: line 005 proves that Haze of Rage with buyback plus Storm-Kiln Artist goes mana-positive once three spells have been cast — each recast returns the card to hand, mints more Treasures than the next cast costs, and pumps the whole team another +1/+0 per copy, without bound. Two casts already leave nine Treasures and a 20/2 Storm-Kiln Artist. From there you assemble the kill yourself: trample via Fists of Flame, tokens-into-Tremors via Empty the Warrens off the Treasure mana, or a Grapeshot riding the storm count the loop keeps raising. If the first wave fails, the deck rebuilds: Past in Flames and Faithless Looting recycle the chain, Goblin Dark-Dwellers rebuys a cheap spell, and Goblin Matron and Moggcatcher find the missing piece.

combo_lines.001: This is the deck's signature trick, verified step by step against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update). The scene: Zada, Hedron Grinder and four Goblin tokens on your battlefield, one red mana open, Crimson Wisps in hand. You cast Crimson Wisps targeting only Zada. Her ability triggers and, on resolution, creates one copy of the spell for each other creature you control — all four tokens are legal targets, so four copies hit the stack, each aimed at a different Goblin. Two rules details matter and are worth memorizing: the copies are put on the stack, not cast, so Zada does not re-trigger and they add nothing to your storm count; and each copy resolves in full, delivering the draw as well as the buff. The final tally for one mana and one card: five cards drawn, and all five of your creatures are red with haste until end of turn. Every one-target cantrip in the deck follows this same blueprint.
combo_lines.002: This is the storm half of the deck doing exactly what the manual promised, verified step by step against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update). The scene: Impact Tremors on your battlefield, four Mountains, and a graveyard that tells the story of the turn so far — Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, and Dragon Fodder, three spells already cast. You cast Empty the Warrens as the fourth. Storm triggers on the cast and counts the three spells cast before it, so three copies join the original on the stack — and here is the detail worth memorizing: those copies are put on the stack, not cast. Four resolutions later you have eight Goblin tokens, and Impact Tremors has triggered once per body for 8 damage to each opponent (32 down to 24, 28 down to 20). The not-cast rule then cuts the other way: when you fire Grapeshot later in the turn, the storm copies add nothing to its count. Grapeshot is the fifth spell cast, sees a storm count of four, and delivers five total instances of 1 damage. Count your casts, not your resolutions.
combo_lines.003: This is the go-tall kill, verified step by step against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update) — and it took the checker two passes to bless it, for a reason worth learning from. The scene: Zada, Hedron Grinder and four Goblin tokens, one opponent at 30 life behind a lone untapped 2/2, two cards already drawn this turn, and Fists of Flame cast for {1}{R} targeting only Zada. Her trigger makes four copies — not cast, so she doesn't re-trigger — and they resolve before the original, each one drawing a card first and then applying its buff. The crucial rule: each copy's +1/+0-per-card value is determined once, on its own resolution, and never grows retroactively when later draws happen. So the buffs lock in ascending — +3, +4, +5, +6 on the tokens, +7 on Zada herself — leaving you five cards deeper and staring at 32 power of trample. The blocker absorbs at most 2, at least 30 tramples through: exactly lethal. And that exactness is why the checker demanded a revision — the first draft skipped the state-based action check. Combat damage doesn't kill anyone by itself; the game checks state-based actions before anyone gets priority, sees a player at 0 or less life, and only then is the game over. When your math comes out exactly lethal, walk that last step every time.
combo_lines.004: This line exists because the manual checks the database's homework — and this time the database lost. The combo graph, citing Commander Spellbook, promises that Krenko, Mob Boss plus Skirk Prospector plus Goblin Warchief makes infinite tokens, infinite mana, and infinite storm. Verified step by step against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update), it does not — not in this deck. The claimed loop recasts Krenko over and over by looping him through the command zone, and the rule that enables that (903.9a) applies only to a commander. Your commander is Zada; Krenko is a regular card, so if he ever hits the graveyard, he stays there. And the loop can't even repeat on the battlefield: his ability costs {T}, nothing here untaps him, and only untapped permanents can be tapped — one activation per turn, full stop. So here is what the line actually is, and it's still excellent: with Warchief out, Krenko costs {1}{R}{R}, has haste, and taps immediately; on the example board of five Goblins, one activation makes five more — ten Goblins, thirteen power, all hasty, storm count a humble one. Skirk Prospector can then convert the seven tokens into seven one-shot red mana while keeping the whole engine (the mana empties at end of phase, so spend it now). Two standing orders: this is a burst, not a loop — plan the turn around one activation — and never, ever sacrifice Krenko to Prospector. The rules have confirmed he does not come back.
combo_lines.005: Here it is: the deck's first verified true infinite, checked step by step against the comprehensive rules (June 19, 2026 update). The scene: Storm-Kiln Artist, three Goblin tokens, four Mountains, three spells already cast, and Haze of Rage cast with buyback as the fourth. Storm makes three copies — put on the stack, not cast — and Storm-Kiln's magecraft pays you for the cast and each copy: four Treasures. Every copy pumps the team +1/+0, but only the original card returns to your hand via buyback; the copies wink out of existence the moment they leave the stack. Recast it and everything scales: cast two is the fifth spell, makes four copies, mints five Treasures. Two casts in, you hold Haze of Rage, own nine Treasures, and Storm-Kiln Artist is a 20/2. The engine math, verified: iteration k costs four mana and yields k+3 Treasures — net positive from cast three onward and strictly better every time. Treasures are mana abilities, so nobody can respond to the payment. That's unbounded Treasures, mana, storm count, and team power — but note the loop itself touches no opponent, and your arbitrarily large team has no haste or evasion from it. The kills are lines you assemble, not verified sequences: Fists of Flame for trample on a titan, the Treasure mana poured into Empty the Warrens under Impact Tremors, or a Grapeshot riding the storm count each real cast raised. Pick your exit before you start looping.

card_roles.Zada, Hedron Grinder: The engine. Any instant or sorcery cast targeting only Zada gets copied for each other creature you control, each copy hitting a different creature — with a token board, your cantrips become mass draw. The combo graph pairs her with Storm-Kiln Artist, and the synergy graph flags Frontline Heroism as her in-deck understudy.
card_roles.Crimson Wisps: The star of verified line 001: one red mana, targets only Zada, and the whole team turns red and hasty while you draw a card per creature. The best single spell in the deck on a wide board.
card_roles.Expedite: Same blueprint as Crimson Wisps — one target, haste, draw a card. Aimed only at Zada, it converts your board into cards and a surprise alpha strike.
card_roles.Renegade Tactics: A one-mana 'can't block' cantrip with a single target, which makes it Zada fuel: mass evasion for the horde plus a card per creature.
card_roles.Ancestors' Aid: Pump plus a Treasure on a single-target instant — it qualifies for Zada's trigger, so on a big board it doubles as a first-strike anthem and a mana injection.
card_roles.Fists of Flame: The go-tall payoff: draw a card, then the target gains trample and +1/+0 for each card you've drawn this turn. Save it for the turn you've been drawing in bulk — it targets one creature, so Zada's trigger applies.
card_roles.Wild Ride: One-target haste and +3/+0 with a graveyard rebuy via harmonize; another spell that fits Zada's 'targets only' requirement.
card_roles.Frontline Heroism: Zada's apprentice per the synergy graph (Copy + ETB): every spell you cast at a single creature you control mints a hasty Soldier and copies the spell onto it, snowballing your target count.
card_roles.Dragon Fodder: Two Goblins for two mana. Bodies for Zada copies, Impact Tremors triggers, and sacrifice fodder — the simplest card in the deck and one of the most important.
card_roles.Krenko's Command: Dragon Fodder's twin: two more 1/1 Goblins, same job.
card_roles.Empty the Warrens: Storm token flood — every spell cast before it this turn makes another pair of Goblins. The natural crescendo of a ritual-and-cantrip chain.
card_roles.Mogg War Marshal: Three bodies stapled to one card — a token when he enters and another when he dies — which is why the synergy graph rates him the deck's best sacrifice fodder (in-deck pairing with Goblin Trashmaster).
card_roles.Siege-Gang Commander: Three tokens on arrival, then a sac outlet that turns Goblins into 2-damage bolts. The synergy graph pairs him with Redcap Gutter-Dweller's token-and-sacrifice engine.
card_roles.Siege-Gang Lieutenant: Two hasty tokens every combat while your commander is out, plus a cheap sac-to-ping ability — the synergy graph pairs it with Redcap Gutter-Dweller as well.
card_roles.General Kreat, the Boltbringer: Attacking Goblins bring a friend, and every other creature that enters pings each opponent — a second Impact Tremors on legs. Combo graph partners: Goblin Bombardment, Goblin Chieftain, Goblin Warchief.
card_roles.Searslicer Goblin: Raid: a free Goblin every end step you attacked. Cheap, relentless board growth.
card_roles.Howlsquad Heavy: Haste for the tribe, a token every combat, and at max speed he taps for a red per Goblin — ritual and lord in one. Combo graph partners: Krenko and Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Redcap Gutter-Dweller: Two tokens on arrival, then an upkeep sacrifice that grows him and exiles a card you can play — the synergy graph's in-deck partner for both Siege-Gangs' sacrifice appetites.
card_roles.Impulsive Pilferer: Leaves a Treasure when it dies and Encores from the graveyard for three more bodies. Combo graph partners: Goblin Bombardment and Skullclamp — this is a card that wants to die.
card_roles.Goblin Bushwhacker: Kicked, he gives the team +1/+0 and haste — the classic token-swarm finisher for the turn Empty the Warrens goes wide.
card_roles.Goblin Chieftain: Haste lord: other Goblins get +1/+1 and swing immediately. Combo graph partners: Krenko, General Kreat, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Goblin Warchief: Goblin spells cost less and everything hastes — half ramp, half lord. Combo graph partners: Krenko, General Kreat, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Goblin Trashmaster: A lord who eats Goblins to destroy artifacts. The synergy graph pairs him with Mogg War Marshal — sacrifice the token, keep the value.
card_roles.Rundvelt Hordemaster: Lord plus a card-advantage engine: every Goblin death exiles a card, and Goblin creature cards among them can be cast. Turns board wipes into card flow. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Quest for the Goblin Lord: Five Goblin arrivals turn this one-mana enchantment into a permanent +2/+0 anthem. In this deck, five arrivals is a Tuesday.
card_roles.Goblin Lackey: Connect once and put any Goblin permanent from your hand straight onto the battlefield — a turn-one threat that demands an answer.
card_roles.Goblin Matron: Fetches whatever Goblin the moment calls for — Krenko for tokens, Skirk Prospector for mana, Bushwhacker for the kill.
card_roles.Gempalm Incinerator: Removal disguised as a Goblin: cycle it to deal damage to a creature equal to your Goblin count, and draw a card doing it.
card_roles.Goblin Dark-Dwellers: A menacing body that recasts a 3-or-less instant or sorcery from your graveyard for free — a second helping of Grapeshot, Faithless Looting, or a Zada cantrip.
card_roles.Grenzo, Havoc Raiser: Every creature that connects lets you goad a blocker or cast the top of an opponent's library — with a token horde, that's several triggers per combat.
card_roles.Broadside Bombardiers: A Boast sac outlet with menace and haste: trade a spare token or artifact for damage equal to 2 plus its mana value. The synergy graph places it squarely in the sacrifice cluster.
card_roles.Goblin Bombardment: The premier sacrifice outlet — every creature is a ping, no mana required. The combo graph's busiest hub: partners with Krenko, Impact Tremors, General Kreat, Impulsive Pilferer, Mana Geyser, Roaming Throne, and Sol Ring.
card_roles.Pashalik Mons: Every Goblin death becomes a damage ping, and he can eat a Goblin to make two more. With Bombardment out, your board is a machine gun. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Boggart Shenanigans: Quietly turns every Goblin funeral into a point of damage at any player or planeswalker — pure reach for the attrition game.
card_roles.Skirk Prospector: Goblins are mana — verified in line 004 as a true mana ability: no stack, no responses, activatable mid-payment. On the example board he converts seven spare tokens into seven one-shot red mana (spend it before the phase ends). The combo graph's biggest hub with nine in-deck partners, but the rules say the Krenko pairing is a burst, not a loop — feed him tokens, never the engine.
card_roles.Skullclamp: One mana turns any 1/1 token into two cards. In a token deck this is a card-advantage engine, and the combo graph pairs it with Impulsive Pilferer for extra credit.
card_roles.Battle Hymn: Ritual that scales with your board: add a red per creature you control. The setup spell for storm turns.
card_roles.Brightstone Ritual: Add a red for every Goblin on the battlefield — note it counts all Goblins, not just yours.
card_roles.Mana Geyser: Late in a turn cycle, opponents' tapped lands turn into a mountain of red mana. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Seething Song: Three mana in, five out. Combo graph partners: Ruby Medallion and Storm-Kiln Artist — discounts and Treasures make it even better.
card_roles.Ruby Medallion: Every red spell costs one less, which in a deck of one- and two-mana spells effectively doubles your storm turn. Combo graph partners: Seething Song, Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Fast mana, no notes. Even the combo graph found it a partner here (Goblin Bombardment).
card_roles.Grapeshot: The storm kill: one damage per spell cast before it this turn, aimable anywhere. The payoff at the end of every ritual-and-cantrip chain.
card_roles.Haze of Rage: One half of the deck's verified infinite (line 005): buyback returns the card to hand every cast, storm multiplies it, and with Storm-Kiln Artist out each iteration mints more Treasures than the next cast costs — unbounded mana, storm count, and team pump. Even off-loop, it's a storm anthem. Combo graph partners: Storm-Kiln Artist and Throne of Eldraine.
card_roles.Spreading Insurrection: Storm Threaten: steal an untapped, hasty creature per copy. Turns the table's best boards against them on your combo turn.
card_roles.Storm-Kiln Artist: The paymaster and the other half of the verified infinite: a Treasure for every instant or sorcery you cast or copy — Zada copies and storm copies both count, as line 005 proves. Its +1/+0-per-artifact static means the loop also turns it into a giant (a 20/2 after just two Haze casts). Combo graph partners: Zada herself, Haze of Rage, and Seething Song.
card_roles.Past in Flames: The rebuild button: your whole graveyard of rituals and cantrips gains flashback for a turn. Cast your storm twice.
card_roles.Faithless Looting: Draw two, discard two, flashback later — smooths early hands and stocks the graveyard for Past in Flames and Dark-Dwellers.
card_roles.Glimpse the Impossible: Impulse three cards off the top; anything you don't use becomes Eldrazi Spawn tokens that sacrifice for mana — card flow that leaves bodies behind.
card_roles.Witch's Mark: Loot away a dead card to draw two, and pin a Wicked Role on a creature so its eventual death stings each opponent.
card_roles.Idol of Oblivion: Tap for a card every turn you made a token — in this deck, that's nearly every turn.
card_roles.Great Train Heist: The modal haymaker: untap the team and take an extra combat, add first strike, or turn combat damage into Treasures — or all three on the turn that ends the game.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: The reset: 13 damage to every creature, usually for one or two mana thanks to your own swarm. With Pashalik Mons or Boggart Shenanigans out, it's also a burn spell.
card_roles.Vandalblast: One-sided artifact sweeper via overload — the answer to Treasure decks and mana rocks that doesn't touch your own Skullclamp.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for the creature everything revolves around. Boot up Zada before you commit to the big turn.
card_roles.Throne of Eldraine: Four red mana in one activation, or three mana and a tap for two cards. Combo graph partner: Haze of Rage.
card_roles.Reliquary Tower: No maximum hand size — the card that lets a five-draw Zada turn actually stick.
card_roles.War Room: A land that draws cards for three mana and a life. Mono-red keeps the price low.
card_roles.Arena of Glory: Taps for one red normally, or exert it for two red that grants a creature spell haste — a ritual you replay every other turn.
card_roles.Castle Embereth: A pump land: +1/+0 to the team at instant speed, which on twenty tokens is twenty extra damage.
card_roles.Den of the Bugbear: A creature-land that attacks as a 3/2 and brings a tapped, attacking Goblin token with it.
card_roles.Dwarven Mine: Enters untapped with three other Mountains and leaves a free 1/1 behind — a land that feeds the swarm.
card_roles.Kher Keep: Endless 0/1 Kobold tokens — cheap bodies for Zada targets and sacrifice outlets.
card_roles.Fountainport: Utility land that sacrifices spare tokens for cards, makes Fish chump-blockers, or mints Treasures.
card_roles.Goblin Burrows: Gives one Goblin +2/+0 per activation — spare-mana reach in the late game.
card_roles.Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep: First strike on demand for a legendary creature — Zada, Krenko, Kreat, or Grenzo swing safer.
card_roles.Spinerock Knoll: Hideaway: stash a spell, then cast it free once an opponent has taken 7 damage in a turn — a bar this deck clears constantly.
card_roles.Hidden Volcano: Late-game land that cashes in for Discover 4 — a spare land becomes a spell.
card_roles.Forgotten Cave: A Mountain early, a card late — cycling smooths the draws.
card_roles.Smoldering Crater: Same deal as Forgotten Cave: land when you need it, card when you don't.
card_roles.Mountain: Twenty-two of them. Every one taps for exactly what the deck wants.
card_roles.Krenko, Mob Boss: Tap: double your Goblin count — a one-shot burst, and the manual has verified exactly that (line 004): the database's 'infinite' Krenko/Prospector loop needs him in the command zone, and here Zada holds that seat, so a sacrificed Krenko is gone for good and he stays tapped after one activation. Play him as five-plus tokens with haste under Warchief, and never sac him to Prospector.
card_roles.Impact Tremors: The quiet killer: one damage to each opponent for every creature that enters. An Empty the Warrens or Krenko activation becomes a fireball to the whole table. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Conspicuous Snoop: Casts Goblins off the top of your library and borrows the top Goblin card's activated abilities. Combo graph partner: Skirk Prospector.
card_roles.Roaming Throne: Name Goblin and every Goblin triggered ability triggers twice — Kreat, Pashalik Mons, Searslicer, Mogg War Marshal, all doubled. Ward 2 keeps it around. Combo graph partner: Goblin Bombardment.
card_roles.Moggcatcher: A repeatable Goblin tutor straight to the battlefield — four mana a turn converts into whichever engine piece you're missing.
card_roles.Chaos Warp: Red's universal answer: shuffle away any permanent, from an enchantment you can't otherwise touch to a problem commander.
card_roles.Daring Discovery: Three attackers can't be blocked and Discover 4 finds you another spell — a pre-combat play that pushes damage and keeps the chain going.
card_roles.Goblin Negotiation: X-damage removal that pays you in Goblin tokens for excess damage — removal that advances the plan.
card_roles.Sazacap's Brew: Sideboard flex, and not the Zada card it looks like: it targets a player, so it never "targets only Zada" and is never copied. Strip that away and it is a two-mana instant that discards as a cost to draw two — card-neutral selection plus one storm count. Do NOT test it in the Witch's Mark slot; Witch's Mark targets a creature and IS copyable. Spreading Insurrection is the slot, against a creature-light pod with no graveyard hate.

mulligan: Keep hands that can do two things: make Goblins early and cast spells cheaply. The gold standard is three lands (or two plus Sol Ring, Skirk Prospector, or Ruby Medallion), a one-or-two-mana token maker — Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Mogg War Marshal, Searslicer Goblin — and a cantrip like Crimson Wisps or Expedite banked for the turn Zada comes down. Zada is always waiting in the command zone at four mana, so your opening hand doesn't need a payoff; it needs bodies and mana. Ship hands that are all crescendo and no verse — Blasphemous Act, Mana Geyser, and Empty the Warrens with two lands is a mulligan, because rituals and storm cards do nothing without a board and a spell count. Faithless Looting and Witch's Mark upgrade marginal keeps by trading dead cards for live ones. One table tip: the sideboard's Red Mana and Storm Counter cards are Secret Lair table aids with no rules text — put them in front of you on big turns to track floating ritual mana and your storm count, because a ten-spell turn is exactly when bookkeeping errors happen. The goldfish numbers back the plan: under the 2-to-5-land keep rule, 79% of first sevens are keepable, and the deck averages its first token maker by turn 3.2 — so a keep with bodies and cheap spells is the statistical default, not a gamble.
upgrades: The obsolescence index flags a number of cards in this list with strictly-better replacements — treat these as prompts, not orders, since the index compares raw function and can't see that this deck cares about the Goblin creature type and about spells that target only one creature. The funniest finding first: Spreading Insurrection is flagged as obsoleted by Grapeshot (lower CMC, similarity 0.98) — a card you already run, which makes Insurrection a natural cut when you find something you like better. The deepest upgrade wells: Gempalm Incinerator is outclassed by Misty Knight, Hero for Hire (cheaper, bigger, similarity 0.996), Spider-Gwen, Free Spirit, and Hawkeye, Master Marksman; Rundvelt Hordemaster by Unlucky Witness (cheaper, 0.997) among several others; and Past in Flames by a cluster of cheaper options led by Firebolt and Kaleidoscorch (0.997) — though weigh what you'd lose there carefully. Elsewhere: Pashalik Mons is bettered by Krenko, Baron of Tin Street (bigger body plus counters, 0.91); Goblin Chieftain by Hero of the Games or the cheaper Hexing Squelcher; Goblin Warchief by Marauding Raptor or Foundry Inspector; Mana Geyser by the cheaper Desolation of Smaug or Dragon's Desire; Idol of Oblivion and Throne of Eldraine both by Daily Bugle Newspaper; Krenko's Command by Cindercone Smite; Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual by Guild Pact; Crimson Wisps and Expedite by Academic Dispute; Goblin Bushwhacker by Artillery Enthusiast; Goblin Lackey by Kellan, Planar Trailblazer; Searslicer Goblin by Prompto Argentum; General Kreat by Molten Lavamancer or Ultron, Artificial Malevolence; Broadside Bombardiers by Skittering Precursor; and Siege-Gang Commander, Siege-Gang Lieutenant, and Storm-Kiln Artist all by Contract Hero. Before any swap, check the replacement's creature type and targeting text against the deck's two pillars — Goblin tribal counts and Zada's 'targets only' clause. Finally, Sazacap's Brew is already sitting in your sideboard: a cheap instant that trades a discard for two fresh cards, worth testing in a flex slot.
threat_assessment:
The table reads your clock before you do. Zada, Hedron Grinder lands on turn 4 in 70% of games (7,002 of 10,000 goldfish iterations cast her exactly on 4; mean 4.35, median 4, 90% by turn 6). Any opponent who has seen this deck once will count your Mountains and know the turn-4 window is coming. What they can't read is your board before that: on turn 3 you average just 2.36 bodies — a Skirk Prospector and a couple of 1/1 tokens look like chump blockers, not the fuel tank for a draw engine. That gap between what your board says and what your hand is building is your entire early game.

The flip from ignored to archenemy happens at two precise thresholds now, and you should know both cold. The first is Zada untapped, three-plus other creatures, one red mana open: verified stack 001 shows one {R} Crimson Wisps becoming five cards and a hasted board. The second is the deck's true verified infinite — stack 005 proves that Haze of Rage with buyback plus Storm-Kiln Artist, once about three spells have been cast that turn, is a mana-positive loop that strictly improves: iteration k costs four mana and yields k+3 Treasures plus a team-wide +1/+0, and in the verified run two casts made 9 Treasures, three 10/1 Goblins, and a 20/2 Storm-Kiln. The moment Storm-Kiln Artist is on your battlefield with four mana up and Haze in hand, informed opponents must respect lethal — and their counterplay is scripted: kill Storm-Kiln in response to the first magecraft trigger, or hit the Treasures with instant-speed artifact hate. Treat the first Haze cast as the commitment point, and prefer to fire when the table's interaction is tapped or spent. Your other known-card signals stay the same: Skullclamp screams engine deck, and Conspicuous Snoop shows your library top all game.

Sequencing under the radar: deploy token makers early — Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command read as defense, and the goldfish says your early token maker arrives on turn 3.18 on average, comfortably before Zada. Cast Zada as 'just a 3/3' and pass; the full engine assembles by turn 5.27 on average and only 49.6% of the time by turn 6, so you usually get one quiet turn. Never fire a cantrip at Zada for two copies of value. And know what Krenko, Mob Boss actually is here: the combo databases call Krenko plus Prospector plus a haste lord infinite, but stack 004 verifies it is not a loop in this deck — Krenko is not your commander, he stays tapped after one activation, and a Krenko sacrificed to Prospector is simply gone. Play him as a one-activation payoff ({1}{R}{R} under Warchief, five tokens on a modest board, ten Goblins and 13 hasted power), never sacrifice him expecting recursion, and don't burn protection defending a loop you don't have. When an opponent panic-removes Krenko expecting the Spellbook infinite, they've paid a real card for a one-shot — sometimes you let them.

Embrace being the threat only when the turn converts: pace for the median game — the Zada draw engine plus wide pressure — and hold the ceiling as opportunism. The go-decision is arithmetic done before the first spell: count the mana and castable spells in your hand and on your board only; expected draws are a bonus, not a plan. Impact Tremors or Boggart Shenanigans down, Krenko untapped with his partners, a Spinerock Knoll set, or the Haze loop live — those are go signs. The goldfish assembles 'storm payoff plus ritual' in only 15.2% of games, so let the table's fear sit on cards you haven't drawn. The turn you draw five cards in front of three opponents, you are the archenemy — so that turn should also be the turn the table has to answer you or start dying.
matchups:
Sweeper control (Azorius/Esper wraths): your engine is your wrath insurance, not your victim. Stack 001 proves one Crimson Wisps with four bodies banks five cards into a zone the sweeper can't touch, and Storm-Kiln Artist's magecraft mints Treasures that ride straight through a creature wrath — stack 005's 9 Treasures would survive the board dying and fund the rebuild. When the wrath is telegraphed at sorcery speed, the arithmetic changes: go for value now — fire the cantrip engine and bank the draws — rather than holding for a lethal that never gets cheaper. Hold one token maker in hand at all times, keep Past in Flames as your rebuild, and remember Pashalik Mons and Goblin Bombardment convert the wrath itself into a burst of damage on the way down. Mogg War Marshal even dies into another body.

Stax and tax pieces: taxes attack your velocity math directly — recount your hand under the tax, because a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine. One lock piece is an inconvenience; the compounding second and third are the lock, so you rarely own the long game here: you are the beatdown, racing the lock's assembly. Name your outs early and by name — Vandalblast (overload {4}{R}), Goblin Trashmaster ('Sacrifice a Goblin: Destroy target artifact', repeatable), Chaos Warp for enchantments and commanders — and sequence to protect the one that breaks the piece that beats you, not the scariest piece. Ruby Medallion and Goblin Warchief pay the toll, and Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual scale with your board rather than your lands — mana denial hurts less than the table assumes, since your land-drop rate falls to 54% by turn 6 anyway. Even the verified Haze loop survives a modest tax if you redo the math: iteration k yields k+3 Treasures against four mana plus the tax, so under a two-mana sphere the loop turns profitable a couple of casts later, not never.

Aggro and token mirrors: you win these on asymmetry, not size. Gempalm Incinerator cycles to kill their lord for X equal to all Goblins on the battlefield — theirs count too. Blasphemous Act is often {1}{R} in a token mirror; hold it as the reset you're uniquely able to rebuild from (mean 4.07 bodies by turn 5, rituals unmodeled). Stack 004's verified burst is your mirror-breaker: Krenko for {1}{R}{R} under Warchief, one activation, ten Goblins and 13 hasted power from a three-body start — spend it as the one-shot it is. Anthems break stalls, a single buyback Haze into a real storm count pumps your whole team past theirs, and Impact Tremors plus General Kreat drain every opponent without ever attacking into blockers. Let the other token deck be the archenemy; you out-grind them.

Combo tables: your interaction is thin (Chaos Warp, Gempalm Incinerator, Bombardment as trigger-response), so held answers rot — rank their combo proximity above every board threat and plan to disrupt once, cheaply, at the decisive moment. Your own race line is now real but narrow: stack 005 verifies Haze of Rage plus Storm-Kiln Artist as a true infinite, and because every Haze cast is a real cast, the storm count climbs each iteration toward a Grapeshot payout. When you hold both pieces, do the go arithmetic before the first spell: three real casts before Haze makes the loop self-funding — count only hand and board. Without the pieces, the goldfish number stands: payoff-plus-ritual assembles in 15.2% of games, so your realistic clock is wide haste attacks plus Impact Tremors drain, with Grenzo goads pulling their defenses apart. Remember Zada's copies are not cast (rule 707.10) and add nothing to storm. If the table asks whether you're 'the storm deck,' the honest answer: a Goblin aggro deck with a very good draw engine — until Storm-Kiln Artist hits the battlefield.
